subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled: false` become a hard security boundary that denies agent reads and execution from that skill directory, or should OpenClaw keep it as an eligibility-only control with a separate strict isolation policy?
rationale: Both choices are plausible: hard-deny matches user expectations and security wording, but it changes existing semantics and `exec` cannot be made safe by simple command-text filtering.

options.title: Make disabled skills hard-denied
options.body: Treat `enabled:false` as a central deny policy for skill-owned file exposure and document how exec/sandbox deployments must enforce the remaining boundary.

options.title: Add a separate strict isolation mode
options.body: Keep current compatibility for `enabled:false` and add an explicit operator-controlled policy for deployments that need disabled-skill path denial.

options.title: Document eligibility-only semantics
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and update UI/docs to avoid implying disabled skills are sandboxed or inaccessible.

recommendation.title: Make disabled skills hard-denied
recommendation.body: Treat `enabled:false` as a central deny policy for skill-owned file exposure and document how exec/sandbox deployments must enforce the remaining boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is a security/product boundary choice, and recent source plus adjacent skill-install hardening history points to steipete as the best available routing owner.
